analyzed_vuln.description: Use-after-free is caused by incorrect zval lifetime management during compilation of nullsafe property access on a constant array expression. A constant array zval produced via compile-time evaluation (from zend_try_ct_eval_array) is propagated through delayed var/property compilation, and the same underlying array ends up referenced by multiple literals without proper refcount ownership separation. During destroy_op_array(), zval_ptr_dtor_nogc() runs over literals and decrements/frees the array once, then later touches the duplicated stale literal again, triggering UAF in zend_gc_delref.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Trigger with source that builds a constant array and then uses nullsafe property access with an invalid property token, e.g. "<?['']?->\xff;" in php-fuzz-parser. Data flow: fuzzer input -> parser/AST -> zend_compile_expr/zend_compile_var -> zend_delayed_compile_prop (nullsafe path) with constant array from zend_try_ct_eval_array. Compilation error/unwind still leaves duplicated literal ownership state in op_array; when fuzzer_do_request destroys the op_array, literal destruction double-decrefs the same array allocation, causing heap-use-after-free.
